Definition: a prolonged form of the feminine of G3432; an adulteress (literally or figuratively):--adulteress(-ous, -y).
BiblicalUsage: Moichalis is an adulteress — and Jesus turns the word on His own generation: an evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign. James goes further and calls worldly believers adulterers and adulteresses, friends of the world and enemies of God, while Paul uses the married woman to teach how death ends a bond.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word is meant to hurt. Unfaithfulness to God is not a mistake, it is adultery, and naming it plainly is the first step back.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
